title: Grade 4
emphasis: More precise descriptions, motives, and explanations

words.definition: hesitant or not wanting to do something

hero.text: Nova was reluctant to cross the shaky bridge, but she knew someone needed help on the other side.

words.everyday: Mia was reluctant to speak in front of the class.

contrast.nonExample: Sam can't swim yet, so he stays out of the pool.
contrast.explanation: Being unable to do something is different from being reluctant. Someone may be able to swim but still be reluctant to get into cold water.

items.prompt: Which person is reluctant?

options.text: Ava runs over to join the game right away.
Leo hangs back because he doesn't want to join.
Zoe cheers loudly for her team.

items.hint: Look for the person who does not want to do something.
items.explanation: Reluctant means hesitant or unwilling. Leo hangs back because he doesn't want to join.

wrong.a: Ava wants to join immediately, so eager fits her better.
wrong.c: Zoe is excited, not hesitant.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Although he knew how to swim, Ben was ___ to jump into the icy lake.
items.clue: Although he knew how; icy
items.hint: "Although" tells you something unexpected is coming. How might someone feel about icy water?
items.explanation: "Although he knew how to swim" shows Ben was able, and "icy" shows why he hesitated. Reluctant fits: he did not want to jump.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "reluctant" in this sentence?
items.passage: The puppy was reluctant to step onto the slippery floor.
items.hint: Did the puppy not want to, or could it not?
items.explanation: Unwilling means not wanting to, which matches reluctant. Unable means it couldn't, which is a different idea.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what reluctant means.

chunks.text: but she handed one to her friend.
so she happily gave them all away.

items.hint: A reluctant person hesitates. Which ending shows hesitation and then a choice?
items.explanation: Reluctant people hesitate, so "but she handed one to her friend" fits. "Happily gave them all away" shows eagerness, not reluctance.

items.prompt: Which word best describes how Lena felt?
items.passage: Lena eventually agreed to lend out her favorite book, but she hesitated for a long time first.
items.clue: hesitated for a long time
items.hint: What does hesitating before agreeing tell you?
items.explanation: "Hesitated for a long time" before agreeing shows Lena didn't really want to. That is reluctant. Furious is much stronger anger, and nothing shows she was angry.

words.definition: to look at something closely and carefully to find out the facts

hero.text: Pixel investigated the strange glowing footprints, measuring and photographing each one for clues.

words.everyday: Our class investigated why some plants on the windowsill grew taller than the others.

contrast.nonExample: Theo glanced at the puddle on the kitchen floor and walked away without wondering where it came from.
contrast.explanation: Investigating means carefully searching for facts or causes. A quick glance with no questions is not investigating.

items.prompt: What does investigate mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The scientists will investigate why the lake water suddenly turned green.

options.text: to look closely to find the facts
to warn people about a danger
to stop thinking about a problem

items.hint: The scientists want to know why. What do you do when you want to find out why?
items.explanation: Investigate means to look closely and carefully to find out the facts. The scientists want to learn why the water changed color.

wrong.a: Cleaning might come later, but first they want to find out why it happened.
wrong.c: Warning people is telling, not finding out.
wrong.d: This is the opposite: investigating means paying close attention to a problem.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: When the cookies vanished from the jar, Grandpa decided to ___ by checking for crumbs and fingerprints.
items.clue: checking for crumbs and fingerprints
items.hint: Grandpa is looking for clues. What word means searching for facts?
items.explanation: "Checking for crumbs and fingerprints" means looking carefully for clues to find out what happened. That is what it means to investigate.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "investigated" in this sentence?
items.passage: The museum staff investigated how the old painting had been damaged.
items.hint: The staff wanted to find out how the damage happened.
items.explanation: Examined means looked at closely to learn more, which matches investigated. Repaired means fixed; that might come after the investigation, but it is a different action.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what investigate means.

chunks.text: why the team kept losing the ball
by watching videos of every game.
by refusing to think about it at all.

items.hint: Investigating takes careful looking. Which ending shows that?
items.explanation: Watching videos of every game is a careful way to find out the cause, so it shows investigating. Refusing to think about it is the opposite of investigating.

items.prompt: Is Rosa investigating?
items.passage: Rosa wanted to know why her bike chain kept slipping, so she studied it, tested the gears, and read the manual.
items.hint: Is Rosa carefully searching for the reason?
items.explanation: Yes. Rosa studies, tests, and reads to find out why the chain slips. Looking carefully for the cause of a problem is investigating.

words.definition: good at finding clever ways to solve problems with what you have

hero.text: When the power went out, Juniper was resourceful and used glow sticks to light up the shelter.

words.everyday: Without a ruler, the resourceful student measured her desk using a dollar bill.

contrast.nonExample: When his pencil broke, Omar just sat and waited for the teacher to notice instead of looking for another one.
contrast.explanation: A resourceful person finds a way to solve a problem with whatever is nearby. Waiting for someone else to fix it is not resourceful.

items.prompt: Which person is resourceful?

options.text: Kira forgets her umbrella and stays wet all day.
Jon buys a brand-new umbrella every time it rains.
Lia folds a newspaper into a rain hat.
Max complains loudly that it is raining.

items.hint: Who solves the problem cleverly using something already nearby?
items.explanation: Resourceful means finding clever ways to solve problems with what you have. Lia turns a newspaper into a hat.

wrong.a: Kira does nothing to solve the problem.
wrong.b: Buying something new is not using what you already have.
wrong.d: Complaining does not solve the problem.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: With no tape left, the ___ artist held her poster together using paper clips and string.
items.clue: With no tape left; using paper clips and string
items.hint: The artist ran out of something but still found a way. What word fits that?
items.explanation: "With no tape left" is the problem, and "using paper clips and string" is her clever fix. Solving a problem with what is on hand is being resourceful.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what resourceful means.

chunks.text: When the recipe called for buttermilk,
mixed milk with lemon juice instead.
gave up and threw the batter away.

items.hint: A resourceful cook finds a way to keep going. Which ending shows that?
items.explanation: Mixing milk with lemon juice is a clever swap using what was in the kitchen, so it shows resourcefulness. Giving up does not.

items.prompt: A resource is something useful you can use, and -ful means "full of." What does resourceful mean?

options.text: full of ways to use what you have
able to buy whatever you want

items.hint: Put the two parts together: full of + useful things.
items.explanation: Resource + -ful means full of ways to use helpful things. A resourceful person makes good use of whatever is around them.

wrong.b: This describes having nothing, not being clever with what you have.
wrong.c: Having lots of things is not the same as using them cleverly.
wrong.d: Buying is not the same as finding clever ways.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Dev?
items.passage: Stranded without a map on the hiking trail, Dev drew one from memory and used the sun to find north.
items.clue: drew one from memory; used the sun to find north
items.hint: Did good things just happen to Dev, or did he make his own solution?
items.explanation: Dev "drew one from memory" and "used the sun to find north," solving his problem with what he had. That is resourceful. Lucky would mean things went well by chance.

words.definition: something that happens because of an earlier action or choice

hero.text: Bolt forgot to charge his speed boots, and the consequence was a very long walk home.

words.everyday: One consequence of the heavy rain was a soccer field too muddy to play on.

contrast.nonExample: Before the storm arrived, the sky turned dark and the wind began to pick up.
contrast.explanation: Those are signs that come before an event. A consequence comes after, as a result of something that already happened.

items.prompt: Is feeling sleepy a consequence of staying up late?
items.passage: Ella stayed up very late reading, so she felt sleepy during math class the next day.
items.hint: Did the sleepiness happen because of something Ella did earlier?
items.explanation: Yes. The word "so" shows that feeling sleepy happened because Ella stayed up late. A result of an earlier choice is a consequence.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Littering in the park had a serious ___: birds got tangled in the plastic bags.
items.clue: Littering; birds got tangled
items.hint: What happened because people littered?
items.explanation: The birds getting tangled happened because of the littering. Something that results from an action is a consequence.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "consequence" in this sentence?
items.passage: A consequence of skipping breakfast was that Jamal felt hungry all morning.
items.hint: Feeling hungry came after skipping breakfast. Is it the cause or what came from it?
items.explanation: Result means what happens because of something, just like consequence. Cause is the opposite: skipping breakfast was the cause, and feeling hungry was the result.

items.prompt: Which line uses consequence correctly?

options.text: "Please hand me that consequence on the shelf."
"Our garden was a consequence of planting seeds in May."
"The consequence happened before I even made my choice."

items.hint: A consequence comes after an action, because of it.
items.explanation: The garden grew because the seeds were planted, so it is a consequence of planting. A consequence is not an object to hand someone, and it cannot happen before the choice that causes it.

wrong.a: A consequence is an outcome, not a thing on a shelf.
wrong.c: A consequence comes after the choice, not before.

items.prompt: What was a consequence of cutting down the trees?
items.passage: The town cut down most of the trees on the hill. Later, heavy rains washed thick mud into the streets below.
items.clue: Later, heavy rains washed thick mud
items.hint: Which thing happened later, because of what the town did?
items.explanation: "Later" tells you the mud came after the trees were cut. Without tree roots to hold the soil, mud washed down. That result is a consequence. The town's decision was the cause.

words.definition: exactly correct, with no mistakes

hero.text: Kai's map of the tunnels was so accurate that the team found the exit in minutes.

words.everyday: The nurse used a special scale to get an accurate measurement of the baby's weight.

contrast.nonExample: Lucy guessed that the jar held about a hundred marbles without counting any of them.
contrast.explanation: A guess might be close, but accurate means exactly right, usually after careful checking or measuring.

items.prompt: Which statement is accurate?

options.text: Ada says the bus comes at 3:00, but it comes at 3:30.
Tim says there are six eggs, but there are only four.
Ben says the movie starts at 7:00, and it does.

items.hint: Which person's information turns out to be exactly right?
items.explanation: Accurate means exactly correct. Ben said 7:00, and the movie really started at 7:00.

wrong.a: Ada was off by thirty minutes, so she was not accurate.
wrong.b: Tim counted wrong, so his count was not accurate.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The scientist checked her numbers three times to make sure the results were ___.
items.clue: checked her numbers three times
items.hint: Why would someone check numbers again and again?
items.explanation: People check numbers "three times" to be sure there are no mistakes. Results with no mistakes are accurate.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "accurate" in this sentence?
items.passage: The weather report was accurate: it said rain at noon, and it rained at noon.
items.hint: An accurate report is right. What is the opposite of right?
items.explanation: Accurate means exactly right, so its opposite is wrong. Correct means the same as accurate, not the opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what accurate means.

chunks.text: because she guessed at most of the facts

items.hint: What makes a story exactly correct?
items.explanation: Checking every fact with two sources is how you make sure there are no mistakes, so the story is accurate. Guessing at facts leads to mistakes, not accuracy.

items.prompt: Is the hallway clock accurate?
items.passage: The clock in the school hallway runs ten minutes fast, so students keep arriving at lunch too early.
items.hint: Does the clock show exactly the right time?
items.explanation: No. A clock that is ten minutes fast shows the wrong time. Accurate means exactly correct.

words.definition: to respect and look up to someone or something because it is good or impressive

hero.text: The younger students admire Rex because he always helps others, even when nobody is watching.

words.everyday: Many people admire Harriet Tubman for her courage in leading others to freedom.

contrast.nonExample: Jada felt jealous of her friend's new bike and wished it belonged to her instead.
contrast.explanation: Admiring means respecting something good about someone. Jealousy means wanting what someone else has, often with unhappy feelings.

items.prompt: What does admire mean in this sentence?
items.passage: I admire my aunt because she taught herself to speak three languages.

options.text: to respect and look up to

items.hint: Learning three languages is impressive. How do you feel about someone impressive?
items.explanation: Admire means to respect and look up to someone. Teaching yourself three languages is impressive, so the speaker admires her aunt.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Visitors stopped to ___ the giant sand castle, praising every tower and tunnel.
items.clue: praising every tower and tunnel
items.hint: The visitors are praising the castle. What are they doing?
items.explanation: "Praising every tower and tunnel" shows the visitors think the castle is impressive. Looking at something with respect and delight is admiring it.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: Wen thinks her coach is wise and hardworking, and she hopes to be like her someday. Wen ___ her coach.
items.clue: wise and hardworking; hopes to be like her
items.hint: Wen respects her coach and wants to be like her.
items.explanation: Wanting to be like someone because they are wise and hardworking is admiring them. Envies means wanting what someone has, with unhappy feelings. Notices is just seeing, with no respect involved.

items.prompt: Which line uses admire naturally?

options.text: "I admire the rain because it ruined our picnic."
"I admire how patient you are with your brother."
"I admire my homework, so I hid it under the bed."

items.hint: We admire things we think are good or impressive.
items.explanation: Patience is a good quality, so admiring it makes sense. People do not admire something for ruining their fun, and hiding homework does not show respect for it.

wrong.a: "Ruined our picnic" is a bad thing, so admire does not fit.
wrong.c: Hiding something does not show you look up to it.

items.prompt: Does Marco admire his classmate's painting?
items.passage: Marco rolled his eyes when his classmate won the art contest and said her painting was boring.
items.hint: Does rolling your eyes show respect?
items.explanation: No. Rolling his eyes and calling the painting boring shows Marco does not respect it. To admire something, you have to think it is good or impressive.

words.definition: worried or nervous about something that might happen

hero.text: Before her first flying test, Juniper felt anxious and kept checking the straps on her cape.

words.everyday: Leo felt anxious the night before the spelling bee and could not fall asleep.

contrast.nonExample: Ana was angry that her brother had eaten the last slice of pizza.
contrast.explanation: Angry is about something that already happened and upset you. Anxious is worry about something that might happen.

items.prompt: Is Priya anxious?
items.passage: Priya keeps checking the clock and biting her nails while she waits for her test results.
items.hint: What do checking the clock and biting nails show about how she feels?
items.explanation: Yes. Checking the clock and biting her nails show Priya is worried about results she does not know yet. Worry about what might happen is being anxious.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The farmer grew ___ as weeks passed with no rain and his crops began to wilt.
items.clue: no rain; crops began to wilt
items.hint: How would you feel if your plants were dying and you didn't know if rain would come?
items.explanation: "No rain" and "crops began to wilt" give the farmer good reason to worry about what will happen. That worried feeling is anxious.

items.prompt: Which word best describes how Sam feels?
items.passage: Sam is a little worried that he might forget his lines in the school play tomorrow.
items.clue: a little worried; might forget
items.hint: Sam is only a little worried. Pick a word that is not too strong.
items.explanation: Anxious means worried about something that might happen, which matches "a little worried." Terrified is much stronger fear, too strong for Sam's feelings.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what anxious means.

chunks.text: when my little sister was late
coming home from her friend's house.
and smiled as she took a calm nap.

items.hint: Anxious people are worried. Which ending gives Mom something to worry about?
items.explanation: A child coming home late is a reason to worry, so it explains why Mom felt anxious. Smiling and napping calmly is the opposite of anxious.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "anxious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The anxious puppy paced back and forth by the door until its owner came home.
items.hint: The puppy is pacing with worry. What is the opposite of worried?
items.explanation: Pacing shows the puppy is worried. The opposite of anxious is calm. Nervous means almost the same as anxious, so it is not the opposite.

words.definition: short in time or length

hero.text: Bolt gave a brief speech, just two sentences long, before the team rushed off to help.

words.everyday: After a brief rain shower, the sun came out and dried the sidewalk.

contrast.nonExample: The movie lasted almost three hours, and some people in the audience fell asleep.
contrast.explanation: Brief means short. Something that goes on for hours is long, not brief.

items.prompt: Which one is brief?
items.hint: Brief means short. Which one takes the least time?
items.explanation: Brief means short in time or length. Five seconds is a very short time.

wrong.a: A summer vacation lasts weeks, which is long.
wrong.b: Ten chapters is a long book, not a brief one.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Our visit with Grandma was ___ because our train left only twenty minutes later.
items.clue: only twenty minutes later
items.hint: How long could the visit last if the train left so soon?
items.explanation: "Only twenty minutes" means there was very little time, so the visit was short. Brief means short. Endless is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "brief" in this sentence?
items.passage: The principal made a brief announcement before lunch and then let us eat.
items.hint: Brief is about how long something lasts.
items.explanation: Brief means short. An announcement could also be loud or important, but those words describe something else, not its length.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what brief means.
items.hint: A brief summary is short. Which length is short?
items.explanation: Three sentences is short, so it matches brief. Ten pages is long, which is the opposite of brief.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the hummingbird's visit?
items.passage: The hummingbird landed on the feeder for only a moment before zooming away over the fence.
items.clue: only a moment
items.hint: How long did the bird stay?
items.explanation: "Only a moment" tells you the visit was very short. Brief means short in time. Lengthy means the opposite.

words.definition: to work together with others to reach the same goal

hero.text: Nova and Kai cooperated to lift the fallen tree off the path, each holding one end.

words.everyday: The students cooperated to build a model volcano, with each person handling one part.

contrast.nonExample: Two brothers each built their own sandcastle and refused to share their buckets.
contrast.explanation: Cooperating means working together toward one goal. Working separately and refusing to share is not cooperating.

items.prompt: Are the neighbors cooperating?
items.passage: On cleanup day, the neighbors split up the jobs: some raked leaves while others bagged them.
items.hint: Are they working together toward one goal?
items.explanation: Yes. The neighbors share the work to reach the same goal: a clean neighborhood. Working together like that is cooperating.

items.prompt: The prefix co- means "together," and operate means "to work." What does cooperate mean?
items.hint: Put the two parts together: together + work.
items.explanation: Co- (together) + operate (work) = work together. The prefix co- also appears in co-pilot, a pilot who flies together with another.

wrong.a: Co- means together, so alone is the opposite.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The puzzle was far too big for one person, so the whole family had to ___ to finish it.
items.clue: too big for one person; the whole family
items.hint: If a job is too big for one person, what must a group do?
items.explanation: "Too big for one person" and "the whole family" show that everyone had to work together. That is cooperating. Compete means trying to beat each other, the opposite idea.

items.prompt: Which line uses cooperate correctly?

options.text: "If we cooperate, we can lift this table together."
"I cooperated by doing the whole project by myself."
"Let's cooperate and each refuse to help."

items.hint: Cooperating always involves more than one person helping.
items.explanation: Lifting a table together is working as a team, so cooperate fits. You cannot cooperate by yourself, and refusing to help is the opposite of cooperating.

wrong.b: Doing it all by yourself is working alone, not cooperating.
wrong.c: Refusing to help is not working together.

items.prompt: Which word describes what the relay team did?
items.passage: In the relay race, each runner passed the baton smoothly to the next, and the team won by working as one.
items.clue: passed the baton smoothly; working as one
items.hint: What does "working as one" mean?
items.explanation: "Passed the baton smoothly" and "working as one" show the runners worked together toward the same goal. That is cooperating.

words.definition: to give a lot of your time and effort to something important to you

hero.text: Rex dedicated every afternoon for a month to learning how to control his super strength.

words.everyday: Dr. Ruiz dedicated her career to protecting sea turtles and their nesting beaches.

contrast.nonExample: Ty tried piano for one week and then stopped practicing because it got hard.
contrast.explanation: Dedicating yourself means giving lots of time and effort over a long time. Quitting after a week is not dedication.

items.prompt: What does dedicated mean in this sentence?
items.passage: Mr. Okafor dedicated his weekends to coaching the youth soccer team.

options.text: gave a lot of time and effort to

items.hint: He spends his weekends on coaching. What does that show?
items.explanation: Dedicate means to give a lot of time and effort to something. Mr. Okafor spends his weekends coaching, so he dedicated them to the team.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The volunteers ___ their whole summer to rebuilding the playground after the flood.
items.clue: their whole summer to rebuilding
items.hint: The volunteers spent a long time and lots of effort on one goal.
items.explanation: Giving "their whole summer" to rebuilding means spending lots of time and effort on it. That is dedicating it.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "dedicated" in this sentence?
items.passage: The author dedicated three years to writing her first novel about life on a farm.
items.hint: She spent three years working hard on her book.
items.explanation: Devoted means gave time and effort with care, just like dedicated. Wasted also involves time, but it means using it for nothing, which is not the same.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what dedicate means.

chunks.text: to caring for his vegetable garden.
to forgetting all about his garden.

items.hint: When you dedicate time to something, you put effort into it.
items.explanation: Spending hours caring for a garden shows effort and commitment, which is dedication. You cannot dedicate time to forgetting about something.

items.prompt: Has Aiko dedicated herself to the violin?
items.passage: Aiko signed up for violin lessons but quit after two days because practicing felt boring.
items.hint: Did Aiko give a lot of time and effort over a long time?
items.explanation: No. Quitting after two days means Aiko did not give much time or effort. Dedicating yourself means sticking with something and working hard at it.

words.definition: having made a firm decision and not willing to give up

hero.text: Pixel was determined to fix the broken robot, so she tried again after every failed attempt.

words.everyday: Even after falling off her skateboard twice, Mara was determined to land the new trick.

contrast.nonExample: Will tried the hard puzzle once, sighed, and put it back in the box for good.
contrast.explanation: A determined person keeps going even when something is hard. Giving up after one try is not determined.

items.prompt: Which person is determined?

options.text: Isa quits the race when she gets a cramp.
Noor practices free throws until she makes ten.
Jake plays whatever game his friends pick.

items.hint: Who sets a goal and keeps going until she reaches it?
items.explanation: Determined means having a firm goal and not giving up. Noor keeps practicing until she reaches her goal of ten shots.

wrong.a: Isa gives up, which is the opposite of determined.
wrong.c: Jake goes along with others; he has not made a firm decision of his own.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Though the trail was steep and rocky, the ___ climbers kept going until they reached the top.
items.clue: Though the trail was steep; kept going until they reached the top
items.hint: The climbers did not stop even though it was hard.
items.explanation: "Though the trail was steep" shows it was hard, and "kept going until they reached the top" shows they would not give up. That is determined.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Ravi?
items.passage: Ravi made up his mind to finish the marathon, and he kept running even when his legs ached.
items.clue: made up his mind; kept running even when his legs ached
items.hint: Ravi did more than wish. He decided and kept going.
items.explanation: "Made up his mind" and "kept running even when his legs ached" show a firm decision and refusing to quit. That is determined. Hopeful only means wishing something will happen.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what determined means.

chunks.text: until it found its buried bone.
for one second, then lost interest.

items.hint: Determined means not giving up. Which ending shows that?
items.explanation: Digging until it found the bone shows the puppy would not give up, so it is determined. Losing interest after one second is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Marie Curie in this passage?
items.passage: Marie Curie worked for years in a cold, leaky shed, testing material after material until she discovered new elements.
items.clue: worked for years; testing material after material until
items.hint: She kept working for years in a hard place. What does that show?
items.explanation: "Worked for years" in a cold shed and kept testing "until she discovered" something shows she would not give up. That is determined.

words.definition: in the end, after a long time or after many things happen

hero.text: Kai searched the city all afternoon and eventually found the lost kitten hiding under a bench.

words.everyday: The seed took weeks to sprout, but it eventually grew into a tall sunflower.

contrast.nonExample: The moment the bell rang, Ella jumped up and ran outside to play.
contrast.explanation: Eventually means after a long wait or many steps. Something that happens the instant something else does happens immediately, not eventually.

items.prompt: Did the lock open eventually?
items.passage: Dad tried six different keys on the ring before one finally opened the old lock.
items.hint: Did the lock open right away, or after many tries?
items.explanation: Yes. The lock opened only after six tries. Something that happens in the end, after many steps, happens eventually.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The traffic jam lasted over an hour, but we ___ made it to the beach before sunset.
items.clue: lasted over an hour, but
items.hint: They had a long wait first. When did they arrive?
items.explanation: "Lasted over an hour, but" tells you they arrived only after a long delay. That is eventually. Immediately would mean right away, which does not fit a long traffic jam.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "eventually" in this sentence?
items.passage: After many tries, Ana eventually solved the tricky riddle.
items.hint: Eventually means after a long time. What means with no wait at all?
items.explanation: Eventually means in the end, after a long time. Immediately means right away, so it is the opposite. Finally means almost the same as eventually.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what eventually means.

chunks.text: Kim practiced the song every day for a month,
she could play it before she ever practiced.

items.hint: Eventually comes at the end of a long process.
items.explanation: After a month of practice, Kim could play perfectly. That result came at the end of a long time, so eventually fits. Something cannot happen eventually if it happens before the practice even starts.

items.prompt: Which word best completes the summary?
items.passage: At first, the settlers struggled to grow crops in the rocky soil. After years of trying new methods, their farms began to thrive. Summary: The settlers' farms ___ thrived.
items.clue: At first; After years of trying
items.hint: Did the farms do well right away, or after a long time?
items.explanation: "At first" they struggled, and only "after years of trying" did the farms thrive. Success after a long time is eventually. Never is wrong because the farms did thrive.

words.definition: facts or signs that show something is true

hero.text: Rex pointed to the muddy paw prints as evidence that a raccoon had raided the lab snacks.

words.everyday: Scientists found seashell fossils on the mountain, evidence that it was once under the ocean.

contrast.nonExample: Ben thinks his sister ate his cookie just because she seems like the type.
contrast.explanation: That is only a hunch. Evidence is something you can point to that shows what is true, like crumbs on her shirt.

items.prompt: Which one is evidence that it rained last night?

options.text: puddles on the sidewalk this morning
a wish that it will rain tomorrow
a sunny forecast for the weekend

items.hint: Evidence is something you can see that shows what happened.
items.explanation: Evidence is a fact or sign that shows something is true. Puddles you can see this morning show that rain fell last night.

wrong.b: A wish is about the future and shows nothing about last night.
wrong.c: A forecast is about the weekend, not last night.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The detective collected ___, such as fingerprints and a torn ticket, to solve the case.
items.clue: such as fingerprints and a torn ticket; to solve the case
items.hint: Fingerprints and a ticket are clues. What word means clues that prove something?
items.explanation: "Fingerprints and a torn ticket" are signs that can show what really happened. Things that help prove the truth are evidence.

items.prompt: What did Tia use to support her claim?
items.passage: In her essay, Tia supported her claim that recess helps learning by describing a study of 500 students.
items.clue: a study of 500 students
items.hint: A study collects real facts. Is that an opinion or proof?
items.explanation: A study of 500 students gives facts that show her claim is true. That is evidence. An opinion is what someone thinks, and a rumor is something people say that may not be true.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what evidence means.

chunks.text: that the day had grown warm.
that the day had grown colder.

items.hint: Evidence shows what is true. What does melting snow show?
items.explanation: Snow melts when it gets warm, so a melted snowman shows the day grew warm. It cannot be evidence that the day grew colder.

items.prompt: Is Omar giving evidence?
items.passage: Omar says the class hamster escaped because "hamsters just do that sometimes," but he has not checked the cage.
items.hint: Has Omar pointed to any facts or signs?
items.explanation: No. Omar is only guessing and has not looked for any signs. Evidence would be something real, like an open cage door.

words.definition: extremely tired, with no energy left

hero.text: After stacking sandbags all night to stop the flood, Bolt was exhausted and fell asleep standing up.

words.everyday: After running the whole cross-country course, Nia was so exhausted that she lay down in the grass.

contrast.nonExample: Theo yawned a little during the slow movie but still wanted to play tag afterward.
contrast.explanation: Feeling a little sleepy is not the same as exhausted. Exhausted means completely worn out, with no energy left.

items.prompt: Is Mom exhausted?
items.passage: After moving heavy boxes all day, Mom could barely lift her arms and fell asleep on the couch.
items.hint: Does Mom have any energy left?
items.explanation: Yes. Barely lifting her arms and falling asleep show Mom has no energy left. That is exhausted.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: After swimming fifty laps without a break, Lucy could hardly climb out of the pool. She was ___.
items.clue: fifty laps without a break; could hardly climb out
items.hint: Lucy is more than a little tired. Pick the strongest tired word.
items.explanation: "Could hardly climb out" after fifty laps shows Lucy used up all her energy. Exhausted means extremely tired. Sleepy is much weaker and means ready for bed.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "exhausted" in this sentence?
items.passage: The exhausted hikers rested by the stream before heading home.
items.hint: Exhausted means no energy. What means full of energy?
items.explanation: Exhausted means having no energy left, so the opposite is energetic. Worn out means the same as exhausted.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The new puppy chased balls around the yard for hours and was ___ by bedtime.
items.clue: chased balls for hours
items.hint: How would you feel after running for hours?
items.explanation: Chasing balls "for hours" would use up all the puppy's energy. Being completely worn out is being exhausted.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the runner?
items.passage: The marathon runner crossed the finish line, stumbled, and sank onto a cot. Her legs shook, and she could not even lift her water bottle.
items.clue: stumbled; legs shook; could not even lift her water bottle
items.hint: What do shaking legs and weak arms tell you?
items.explanation: Stumbling, shaking legs, and being unable to lift a water bottle show she has no energy left. That is exhausted.

words.definition: well known to you because you have seen or heard it before

hero.text: Lost in the fog, Nova smiled when she heard the familiar chime of the academy's clock tower.

words.everyday: On the first day at her new school, Aria smiled when she spotted a familiar face from camp.

contrast.nonExample: Ian moved to a new city where every street and store was strange to him.
contrast.explanation: Familiar things are ones you already know. Places you have never seen before are unfamiliar.

items.prompt: What does familiar mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The song on the radio sounded familiar, so Leah started humming along.
items.hint: Leah could hum along. Had she heard it before?
items.explanation: Familiar means known because you have seen or heard it before. Leah could hum along, so she already knew the song.

wrong.c: New and strange is the opposite. Leah could not hum a song she had never heard.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: After driving the same route for three years, the bus driver found every stop ___.
items.clue: the same route for three years
items.hint: What happens when you see the same places again and again?
items.explanation: Driving "the same route for three years" means the driver knows every stop well. Well-known places are familiar. Unusual is the opposite.

items.prompt: The prefix un- means "not." What does unfamiliar mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The hikers felt nervous on the unfamiliar trail and checked their map often.
items.hint: Un- + familiar = not + known.
items.explanation: Un- means not, so unfamiliar means not known. The hikers had never been on this trail, which is why they kept checking their map.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what familiar means.

chunks.text: because I had never been inside it.

items.hint: Something smells familiar when you have smelled it many times.
items.explanation: Smelling the same bread again and again makes the smell well known, so it is familiar. A place you have never been cannot smell familiar.

items.prompt: Was the new country familiar to Mei?
items.passage: On her first visit to a new country, Mei could not read any of the signs and did not recognize the foods.
items.hint: Did Mei already know this place?
items.explanation: No. It was her first visit, and she recognized nothing. Familiar means already well known to you.

words.definition: happening often

hero.text: Juniper makes frequent visits to the city garden, stopping by almost every morning to water the plants.

words.everyday: Our town has frequent thunderstorms in summer, sometimes three in a single week.

contrast.nonExample: A total solar eclipse can be seen from our town only once every few hundred years.
contrast.explanation: That happens very rarely. Frequent means happening often.

items.prompt: Which one is frequent?

options.text: a birthday that comes once a year
a bus that stops every ten minutes
a comet seen once in a lifetime

items.hint: Frequent means often. Which one happens most often?
items.explanation: Frequent means happening often. A bus every ten minutes comes many times a day.

wrong.a: Once a year is not often.
wrong.c: Once in a lifetime is rare, the opposite of frequent.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Because of the ___ power outages, the family kept a flashlight in every room.
items.clue: kept a flashlight in every room
items.hint: Why would a family need flashlights everywhere?
items.explanation: Keeping "a flashlight in every room" makes sense only if the power goes out often. Frequent means happening often. Rare outages would not need so much planning.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "frequent" in this sentence?
items.passage: Mrs. Lee gives frequent spelling quizzes to help us practice.
items.hint: Frequent means often. What means hardly ever?
items.explanation: Frequent means happening often, so the opposite is rare, which means hardly ever. Regular is close in meaning to frequent.

items.prompt: Which line uses frequent correctly?

options.text: "I go every Saturday, so I'm a frequent visitor."
"I went to the zoo once, so I'm a frequent visitor there."
"The frequent ending of the movie surprised me."

items.hint: Frequent describes something that happens again and again.
items.explanation: Going every Saturday is often, so frequent fits. Going once is not frequent, and a movie has only one ending, so it cannot be frequent.

wrong.c: An ending happens one time, so frequent does not fit.

items.prompt: Which word describes how often hummingbirds eat?
items.passage: Hummingbirds must feed every few minutes during the day because their tiny bodies burn energy so fast.
items.clue: every few minutes
items.hint: How often is every few minutes?
items.explanation: "Every few minutes" means the birds eat very often. Frequent means happening often.

words.definition: to pause before doing or saying something because you are unsure

hero.text: Kai hesitated at the edge of the roof, unsure if the jump was safe, then chose the stairs.

words.everyday: When the teacher asked who knocked over the paint, Jordan hesitated before raising his hand.

contrast.nonExample: The moment the whistle blew, Lucia dove straight into the pool.
contrast.explanation: Hesitating means pausing because you are unsure. Diving in instantly shows no pause at all.

items.prompt: Did Ruby hesitate?
items.passage: Before answering the hard question, Ruby paused, bit her lip, and thought for a while.
items.hint: Did Ruby stop before she answered?
items.explanation: Yes. Ruby paused because she was unsure of the answer. Pausing before acting or speaking is hesitating.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Max ___ at the door of the new classroom, unsure if he was in the right place.
items.clue: unsure if he was in the right place
items.hint: What do you do at a door when you are not sure you should go in?
items.explanation: "Unsure if he was in the right place" explains why Max paused. Pausing because you are unsure is hesitating.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: When asked to try the strange green soup, Elena ___ for a moment, then took a tiny sip.
items.clue: for a moment, then took a tiny sip
items.hint: Elena did try the soup in the end. Did she say no, or just pause?
items.explanation: Elena paused "for a moment" and "then took a tiny sip," so she hesitated. Refused would mean she said no and did not try it at all.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what hesitate means.

chunks.text: at the edge of the road,

items.hint: A deer that hesitates stops before moving on.
items.explanation: Looking both ways before crossing shows the deer paused, unsure if it was safe. Dashing across without stopping is the opposite of hesitating.

items.prompt: What does "don't hesitate" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: If you need help with your science project, please don't hesitate to ask me.
items.hint: The speaker wants you to feel free to ask.
items.explanation: To hesitate is to hold back because you are unsure. "Don't hesitate to ask" means ask right away without holding back.

words.definition: to recognize and name who or what something is

hero.text: Pixel used her scanner to identify the strange purple plant as a harmless kind of fern.

words.everyday: The bird-watching club learned to identify robins by their orange chests and cheerful songs.

contrast.nonExample: Gabe saw a bird fly past the window but had no idea what kind it was.
contrast.explanation: Seeing something is not the same as identifying it. To identify means you can recognize and name exactly what it is.

items.prompt: What does identify mean in this question?
items.passage: Can you identify the main character in this story?
items.hint: The question wants you to say who the main character is.
items.explanation: Identify means to recognize and name who or what something is. The question asks you to name the main character.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Using a field guide, the class was able to ___ every kind of leaf they collected on the walk.
items.clue: Using a field guide; every kind of leaf
items.hint: A field guide helps you figure out what something is called.
items.explanation: A field guide shows pictures and names, so the class used it to say what kind each leaf was. That is identifying.

items.prompt: Which line uses identify correctly?

options.text: "I identified the cake by eating all of it."
"Please identify the door so I can walk through."
"I can identify this rock as granite by its speckles."

items.hint: When you identify something, you say what it is.
items.explanation: Using speckles to say the rock is granite is recognizing and naming it, so identify fits. Eating a cake or walking through a door does not name what something is.

wrong.a: Eating the cake does not tell what it is.
wrong.b: You open a door; identifying it would mean saying which door it is.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what identify means.

chunks.text: but still had no idea what it was.

items.hint: If you identify something, you know what it is.
items.explanation: Listening to my lungs helped the doctor recognize the cause, so she identified it. You cannot identify something and still have no idea what it is.

items.prompt: Did Ms. Chen identify the animal?
items.passage: Ms. Chen studied the tracks in the snow and said, "These long back prints were made by a rabbit."
items.hint: Did she name what made the tracks?
items.explanation: Yes. Ms. Chen used the clue of the long back prints to name the animal as a rabbit. Recognizing and naming something is identifying it.

words.definition: able to do things for yourself without needing help or control from others

hero.text: Rex is independent: he packs his own gear and plans his own training without being reminded.

words.everyday: In 1776, the American colonies declared that they would be independent from Britain.

contrast.nonExample: Ella asks her older brother to tie her shoes and pour her cereal every morning.
contrast.explanation: An independent person does things on their own. Needing someone else for everyday tasks is depending on them.

items.prompt: Which person is independent?

options.text: Rosa waits for her dad to pick out her clothes.
Liam makes his own lunch and packs his bag.
Nate copies his friend's answers on every worksheet.

items.hint: Who does things for himself?
items.explanation: Independent means doing things for yourself without help. Liam makes his own lunch and packs his own bag.

wrong.a: Rosa depends on her dad.
wrong.c: Nate depends on his friend's work.

items.prompt: The prefix in- means "not," and depend means "to rely on someone." What does independent mean?

options.text: not needing to rely on others

items.hint: Put the parts together: not + relying on someone.
items.explanation: In- (not) + depend (rely on) = not relying on others. Dependent means relying on others, so in- flips it to the opposite.

wrong.a: This is the meaning of dependent, without the in-.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: After many years of being ruled by another country, the nation finally became ___.
items.clue: being ruled by another country; finally
items.hint: What does a country become when it stops being ruled by someone else?
items.explanation: "Being ruled by another country" is the old situation, and "finally" tells you it changed. A nation that rules itself is independent.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "independent" in this sentence?
items.passage: My cat is very independent and rarely wants to be held or helped.
items.hint: Independent means not needing others. What means needing others?
items.explanation: Independent means not needing help from others, so dependent, which means relying on others, is the opposite. Self-reliant means almost the same as independent.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Ava?
items.passage: Now that she is eleven, Ava rides the city bus to her piano lesson alone and plans her own practice schedule.
items.clue: rides the city bus alone; plans her own practice schedule
items.hint: Does Ava need someone else to do these things for her?
items.explanation: Riding the bus "alone" and planning "her own" schedule show Ava does things for herself. That is independent.

words.definition: to change how someone thinks or acts, or how something happens

hero.text: Nova's calm voice influenced the frightened crowd, and soon everyone was walking safely to the exit.

words.everyday: The amount of sunlight a plant gets can influence how quickly it grows.

contrast.nonExample: Ty's friends begged him to join the band, but he kept his plan to join the chess club.
contrast.explanation: His friends tried, but they did not influence him, because his choice did not change. Influencing means actually changing what someone thinks or does.

items.prompt: What does influenced mean in this sentence?
items.passage: Reading books about astronauts influenced Maya to study science in college.
items.hint: The books changed what Maya decided to do.
items.explanation: Influence means to change how someone thinks or acts. The astronaut books helped shape Maya's choice to study science.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Rainfall and temperature can ___ which crops farmers choose to plant each spring.
items.clue: which crops farmers choose
items.hint: Weather can change the farmers' decision.
items.explanation: Rainfall and temperature help decide "which crops farmers choose." Something that changes a decision influences it.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "influence" in this sentence?
items.passage: A good coach can influence how hard the players work in practice.
items.hint: The coach can change how hard players work.
items.explanation: Affect means to cause a change in something, just like influence. Measure only means finding out how much; it does not change anything.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what influence means.

chunks.text: to start writing her own stories.
but nothing about her changed at all.

items.hint: If something influences you, something about you changes.
items.explanation: Lia started writing because of the author's talk, so the talk changed what she did. That is influence. If nothing changed, she was not influenced.

items.prompt: Did the classmate influence Diego?
items.passage: After a classmate explained how much water is wasted, Diego began turning off the tap while brushing his teeth.
items.hint: Did Diego change what he does after hearing his classmate?
items.explanation: Yes. Diego changed his habit because of what his classmate said. Changing how someone acts is influencing them.

words.definition: to find exactly where something is

hero.text: Bolt used the signal on his wristband to locate Juniper, who was stuck in a stalled elevator.

words.everyday: Using a globe, Sara was able to locate Egypt in the northeast corner of Africa.

contrast.nonExample: Jake wandered around the mall for an hour without ever finding the shoe store.
contrast.explanation: Jake was still searching. To locate something means to actually find exactly where it is.

items.prompt: What does locate mean in this question?
items.passage: Can you locate the library on this map of our town?

options.text: draw a new picture of it

items.hint: You are looking at a map. What do people use maps for?
items.explanation: Locate means to find exactly where something is. On a map, you would point to the spot where the library is.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The lifeguard used binoculars to ___ the swimmer who had drifted far from shore.
items.clue: used binoculars; drifted far from shore
items.hint: Binoculars help you see things far away. What was the lifeguard trying to do?
items.explanation: The swimmer had "drifted far from shore," so the lifeguard "used binoculars" to find exactly where he was. That is locating.

items.prompt: Which line uses locate correctly?

options.text: "I located my keys, but I still don't know where they are."
"Help me locate my keys; they're somewhere in the house."
"I'll locate my keys by hiding them under the couch."

items.hint: When you locate something, you find where it is.
items.explanation: Asking for help to find keys somewhere in the house uses locate correctly. If you located the keys, you would know where they are, and hiding something is the opposite of finding it.

wrong.a: Locating means you now know where they are, so this contradicts itself.
wrong.c: Hiding is not finding.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what locate means.

chunks.text: With help from a metal detector,
the ring he had dropped in the sand.
the ring, which stayed lost forever.

items.hint: If you locate something, it is no longer lost.
items.explanation: Grandpa used the detector to find exactly where the ring was, so he located it. A ring that stays lost forever was never located.

items.prompt: Which word best describes what the sea turtles can do?
items.passage: Sea turtles swim thousands of miles across the ocean and can still find the exact beach where they hatched.
items.clue: find the exact beach
items.hint: Which word means the same as finding the exact place?
items.explanation: "Find the exact beach" means the turtles know exactly where to go. Finding exactly where something is means locating it.

words.definition: very large, heavy, and solid

hero.text: Rex lifted the massive boulder off the road so the school bus could get through.

words.everyday: The blue whale is a massive animal, longer than two school buses parked end to end.

contrast.nonExample: Kim held up a pebble so small that it balanced on her fingertip.
contrast.explanation: A tiny pebble is the opposite of massive. Massive means very big and heavy.

items.prompt: Is the oak tree massive?
items.passage: The old oak tree was so wide that five kids holding hands could not reach around it.
items.hint: Is the tree very big?
items.explanation: Yes. A trunk too wide for five kids to reach around is very large and solid. That is massive.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: It took a giant crane to lift the ___ steel beam to the top of the new building.
items.clue: took a giant crane
items.hint: Why would you need a giant crane to lift something?
items.explanation: Needing "a giant crane" tells you the beam was very big and heavy. That is massive. A tiny beam could be lifted by hand.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "massive" in this sentence?
items.passage: A massive wave crashed onto the beach and soaked everyone on their towels.
items.hint: Massive is about size.
items.explanation: Huge means very big, just like massive. The wave might also have been cold or quick, but those words do not describe size.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what massive means.

chunks.text: were as wide as a trash can lid.

items.hint: A massive animal leaves big footprints.
items.explanation: Footprints as wide as a trash can lid show the elephant is very big and heavy. Footprints smaller than a coin would not match a massive animal.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the Great Pyramid?
items.passage: The Great Pyramid of Giza is built from more than two million stone blocks, and many weigh more than a car.
items.clue: more than two million stone blocks; weigh more than a car
items.hint: Think about how big and heavy two million stone blocks would be.
items.explanation: "Two million stone blocks" that each "weigh more than a car" make the pyramid enormous and heavy. That is massive. Fragile means easily broken, the opposite of solid stone.

words.definition: to put something down and then forget where it is

hero.text: Kai misplaced his mask again and finally found it in the freezer next to the ice cream.

words.everyday: Grandpa often misplaces his reading glasses, even though they are usually on top of his head.

contrast.nonExample: Lily threw her worn-out shoes in the trash on purpose.
contrast.explanation: Misplacing is an accident: you put something down and forget where. Throwing something away on purpose is not misplacing it.

items.prompt: Which person misplaced something?

options.text: Ben gave his old toys to his little cousin.
Ana set down her book and can't remember where.
Cara hung her coat on its usual hook.

items.hint: Who put something down and now can't find it?
items.explanation: Misplace means to put something down and forget where it is. Ana set her book down and can't remember where.

wrong.a: Ben gave the toys away on purpose, so he knows where they went.
wrong.c: Cara put her coat in its usual place, so it is not misplaced.

items.prompt: The prefix mis- means "wrongly" or "badly." Using that clue, what does misplace mean?

options.text: to put down and lose track of
to buy a new place for

items.hint: Mis- + place = put wrongly.
items.explanation: Mis- means wrongly, so misplace means to put something in the wrong spot and lose track of it. Mis- also shows up in misspell (spell wrongly).

wrong.a: Carefully is the opposite of mis-.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Dad always hangs the spare key on the same hook so he won't ___ it again.
items.clue: on the same hook; won't ___ it again
items.hint: Why would someone always put a key in the same spot?
items.explanation: Hanging the key "on the same hook" helps Dad always know where it is, so he won't lose track of it "again." That is misplace.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what misplace means.

chunks.text: my desk, and under my bed.
so I knew exactly where it was.

items.hint: When you misplace something, you have to look for it.
items.explanation: Searching in many places shows I didn't know where my homework was, so I misplaced it. If I knew exactly where it was, it would not be misplaced.

items.prompt: Did Owen misplace his soccer ball?
items.passage: Owen knows his soccer ball is at Liam's house because he left it there on purpose to share.
items.hint: Does Owen know where the ball is?
items.explanation: No. Owen knows exactly where the ball is, and he left it there on purpose. Misplacing means forgetting where you put something.

words.definition: strange and hard to explain or understand

hero.text: A mysterious blue light blinked from the old tower every night, and Pixel wanted to know why.

words.everyday: Nobody in the family could explain the mysterious tapping sound coming from inside the attic wall.

contrast.nonExample: The doorbell rang at three o'clock, and it was the mail carrier, just like every afternoon.
contrast.explanation: Something that is expected and easy to explain is not mysterious. Mysterious things are puzzling and hard to explain.

items.prompt: Is the flower on the desk mysterious?
items.passage: Every morning, a single red flower appeared on Ms. Park's desk, and no one knew who left it.
items.hint: Can anyone explain where the flower comes from?
items.explanation: Yes. "No one knew who left it," so the flower is strange and hard to explain. That is mysterious.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ footprints in the snow stopped in the middle of the field, as if the walker had vanished.
items.clue: stopped in the middle of the field; as if the walker had vanished
items.hint: Footprints that just stop are very strange. What word fits that?
items.explanation: Footprints that end "as if the walker had vanished" are strange and hard to explain. That is mysterious. Ordinary is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "mysterious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The old map had mysterious symbols that no one at the museum could read.
items.hint: No one could figure out the symbols.
items.explanation: Puzzling means hard to understand, just like mysterious. Simple is the opposite, because simple symbols would be easy to read.

items.prompt: Which line uses mysterious correctly?

options.text: "The bus came at 8:00 like always, which was so mysterious."
"The cookies vanished from a locked room. How mysterious!"
"My mysterious sandwich is just ham and cheese, as usual."

items.hint: Mysterious things are hard to explain.
items.explanation: Cookies vanishing from a locked room is strange and hard to explain, so mysterious fits. A bus arriving on time and a usual sandwich are ordinary, not mysterious.

wrong.a: "Like always" means it is expected, not mysterious.
wrong.c: "As usual" means nothing is strange about it.

items.prompt: Which word best describes these disappearances?
items.passage: Sailors once told stories of ships that disappeared in one part of the ocean without a trace, and no one could say why.
items.clue: without a trace; no one could say why
items.hint: Could anyone explain what happened to the ships?
items.explanation: "Without a trace" and "no one could say why" show the disappearances could not be explained. That is mysterious.

words.definition: a person or team you compete against in a game, contest, or argument

hero.text: Before the academy chess tournament began, Juniper shook hands with her opponent, Bolt.

words.everyday: The tennis player watched videos of her opponent to learn how she served the ball.

contrast.nonExample: Mia and Jo run on the same relay team and cheer for each other at every meet.
contrast.explanation: Teammates work on the same side. An opponent is someone on the other side whom you compete against.

items.prompt: What does opponent mean in this sentence?
items.passage: In the spelling bee final, Lucas faced his toughest opponent yet.

options.text: a judge who read the words

items.hint: In a final, who are you trying to beat?
items.explanation: An opponent is someone you compete against. In the final, Lucas faced another speller who was trying to win.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: During the class debate, Ana listened carefully to her ___ and then argued for the other side.
items.clue: debate; argued for the other side
items.hint: In a debate, who argues against you?
items.explanation: In a debate, Ana "argued for the other side," so the person she listened to was on the opposite side. That is her opponent. A teammate would be on her side.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "opponents" in this sentence?
items.passage: Our soccer team shook hands with our opponents after the close game.
items.hint: Opponents play against you. Who plays with you?
items.explanation: Opponents are on the other side, so teammates, who are on your side, are the opposite. Rivals means almost the same as opponents.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what opponent means.

chunks.text: who blocked every move I tried.
who helped me win by playing on my side.

items.hint: An opponent plays against you, not with you.
items.explanation: Blocking my moves shows Grandpa was competing against me, so he was my opponent. Someone playing on my side is a partner, not an opponent.

items.prompt: Is Aaron Sofia's opponent?
items.passage: In the class election, Sofia and Aaron both ran for president, and each tried to win more votes.
items.hint: Are they competing for the same thing?
items.explanation: Yes. Sofia and Aaron are competing to win the same election. Someone you compete against is your opponent, even outside of sports.

words.definition: lasting forever or for a very long time, not meant to change

hero.text: The heroes carved their names into the stone wall as a permanent record of their first rescue.

words.everyday: Be careful with that permanent marker, because it will not wash out of your shirt.

contrast.nonExample: The sandcastle washed away as soon as the tide came in.
contrast.explanation: Something that disappears quickly is temporary. Permanent things last for a very long time.

items.prompt: Which one is permanent?

options.text: a chalk drawing on the sidewalk before a rainstorm
a name carved into a stone monument

items.hint: Which one will still be there many years from now?
items.explanation: Permanent means lasting for a very long time. A name carved into stone can last hundreds of years.

wrong.a: Rain will wash the chalk away.
wrong.b: A soap bubble pops in seconds.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: After two months of moving from hotel to hotel, the family finally found a home that would be ___.
items.clue: moving from hotel to hotel; finally
items.hint: The hotels were short stays. What kind of home were they finally looking for?
items.explanation: "Moving from hotel to hotel" means short stays, and "finally" tells you that changed. A home where they will stay for a long time is permanent. Temporary describes the hotels.

items.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "permanent" in this sentence?
items.passage: The museum's dinosaur display is permanent, so it will be there whenever you visit.
items.hint: Permanent means it stays. What means it is only there for a short time?
items.explanation: Permanent means lasting a long time, so temporary, which means only for a short time, is the opposite. Lasting means almost the same as permanent.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what permanent means.

chunks.text: so it will never fully fade.
so it will be gone by Friday.

items.hint: Something permanent does not go away.
items.explanation: A scar that will never fade lasts forever, so it is permanent. Something gone by Friday is temporary.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the Great Wall?
items.passage: The Great Wall of China was built to last. Some parts of it have stood for more than two thousand years.
items.clue: built to last; stood for more than two thousand years
items.hint: How long has the wall lasted?
items.explanation: "Built to last" and standing "more than two thousand years" show the wall was meant to stay for a very long time. That is permanent.

words.definition: very valuable, or very important and loved

hero.text: Juniper keeps her grandmother's old locket safe because it is the most precious thing she owns.

words.everyday: Clean water is precious in the desert, so families there are careful not to waste a drop.

contrast.nonExample: Ray tossed an old candy wrapper into the recycling bin without a second thought.
contrast.explanation: Something you throw away without caring is not precious. Precious things are valuable or deeply loved.

items.prompt: Is the letter precious to Mira?
items.passage: Mira keeps the first letter her dad ever wrote her in a special box and reads it often.
items.hint: How does Mira treat the letter?
items.explanation: Yes. Keeping the letter in a special box and reading it often shows it is very important and loved. That is precious.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Gold and diamonds are ___ because they are rare and cost a great deal of money.
items.clue: rare; cost a great deal of money
items.hint: Things that are rare and expensive are very ___.
items.explanation: "Rare" and "cost a great deal" show gold and diamonds are very valuable. That is precious. Cheap and plentiful are the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: To the family, the old photo album was ___; it held the only pictures of their great-grandparents.
items.clue: the only pictures of their great-grandparents
items.hint: The album may not cost much money. Why does the family care about it?
items.explanation: The album holds "the only pictures" of loved family members, so it is deeply treasured. Precious can mean loved, not just costly. Expensive is only about money, and an old album probably did not cost much.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what precious means.

chunks.text: on Amir's last day before moving away.
because he didn't care about it at all.

items.hint: Something feels precious when it matters a lot and might not last.
items.explanation: On his last day, time with friends mattered a lot to Amir, so it felt precious. You cannot feel that something is precious if you don't care about it.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "precious" in this sentence?
items.passage: Seeds were precious to the early farmers, who saved them carefully for next year's planting.
items.hint: The farmers saved the seeds carefully. Why?
items.explanation: Valuable means worth a lot, just like precious. Seeds are tiny, but that describes their size, not why the farmers saved them so carefully.

words.definition: coming before in time or order

hero.text: Pixel read her notes from the previous day to remember where she had hidden the spare battery.

words.everyday: Our new teacher asked us to share one thing we had learned in our previous grade.

contrast.nonExample: The next chapter of my book is the one I haven't read yet.
contrast.explanation: Next means coming after. Previous means coming before.

items.prompt: What does previous mean in this sentence?
items.passage: I could not remember the previous question, so I scrolled back up to read it again.

options.text: the last one on the test

items.hint: The person scrolled back up. Was the question before or after?
items.explanation: Previous means coming before. Scrolling back up shows the question came earlier.

wrong.b: Next is the opposite of previous.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Today is Tuesday, so the ___ day was Monday, when we had our spelling test.
items.clue: Today is Tuesday; was Monday
items.hint: Monday comes before Tuesday.
items.explanation: Monday comes right before Tuesday, and "was" shows it is in the past. The day that came before is the previous day. Following would mean Wednesday.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "previous" in this sentence?
items.passage: The previous owner of our house planted the apple tree in the backyard.
items.hint: Did this owner live there before or after us?
items.explanation: Earlier means coming before, just like previous. The previous owner lived in the house before we did. Next is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which line uses previous correctly?

options.text: "I'll see you on the previous Saturday, which is next week."
"On my previous visit, the museum had a dinosaur exhibit."
"The previous chapter is the one I'll read tomorrow."

items.hint: Previous always points back to something earlier.
items.explanation: A previous visit is one that already happened, so this line makes sense. "Next week" and "tomorrow" point to the future, so previous does not fit those lines.

wrong.a: Next week is in the future, not before.
wrong.c: A chapter you will read tomorrow comes after, not before.

items.prompt: Is Ella reading the previous chapter?
items.passage: Ella just finished chapter four, and now she is starting chapter five.
items.hint: Does chapter five come before or after chapter four?
items.explanation: No. Chapter five comes after chapter four, so it is the next chapter. The previous chapter would be chapter three or four, which come before.

words.definition: feeling better because something worrying or painful is over

hero.text: Bolt was relieved when the lost puppy he had been searching for came running out of the alley.

words.everyday: Ava was relieved to hear that her grandma's surgery had gone well.

contrast.nonExample: Ty was excited when he found out his class was going to the zoo next week.
contrast.explanation: Excited means looking forward to something fun. Relieved is the good feeling when a worry finally ends.

items.prompt: Is Jin relieved?
items.passage: Jin had worried all week about his science grade, then smiled and sighed when he saw an A.
items.hint: Jin was worried, and then the worry ended. How does that feel?
items.explanation: Yes. Jin worried all week, and seeing the A ended his worry. That good feeling when a worry is over is relief, so Jin is relieved.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The pilot felt ___ when the storm finally passed and the plane landed safely.
items.clue: storm finally passed; landed safely
items.hint: The danger is over. How would the pilot feel?
items.explanation: "Storm finally passed" and "landed safely" show a scary situation ended well. Feeling better after a worry ends is being relieved.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: When the lights came back on after the scary blackout, Maya let out a long breath. She felt ___.
items.clue: scary blackout; let out a long breath
items.hint: Maya is not cheering. She is calming down after being scared.
items.explanation: Letting out a long breath after something "scary" ends shows relief, not excitement. Excited means eager about something fun ahead. Proud is about something you did well.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what relieved means.
items.hint: Relieved people stop worrying.
items.explanation: "After all" shows the players had been worried, and the good call ended that worry. That is relieved. Worrying even more is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the families?
items.passage: After three days of searching, rescuers found the missing hikers safe and unhurt. Their families hugged one another and cried happy tears.
items.clue: three days of searching; safe and unhurt; happy tears
items.hint: The families were worried for three days. Then what happened?
items.explanation: After "three days of searching," the hikers were found "safe and unhurt," so the families' long worry ended. That is relieved. Anxious describes how they felt before the hikers were found.

words.definition: to need something, or to make something necessary

hero.text: Building the rescue glider required Pixel's math skills and Rex's strength working together.

words.everyday: Most plants require sunlight, water, and air to grow.

contrast.nonExample: Sprinkles are nice on an ice cream cone, but you can enjoy it just fine without them.
contrast.explanation: Something extra is optional. Something required is needed; you cannot do without it.

items.prompt: What does requires mean in this sentence?
items.passage: This pancake recipe requires two eggs and a cup of flour.
items.hint: Can you make the pancakes without the eggs and flour?
items.explanation: Require means to need. The recipe needs eggs and flour to work.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The class trip to the science museum will ___ a permission slip signed by a parent.
items.clue: permission slip signed by a parent
items.hint: Can students go on the trip without the slip?
items.explanation: Schools need a signed permission slip before a trip, so the slip is necessary. Making something necessary is what require means.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "requires" in this sentence?
items.passage: Learning to play the violin well requires a lot of patience and practice.
items.hint: Can you learn violin without patience?
items.explanation: Needs means the same as requires here: you cannot learn violin well without patience and practice.

items.prompt: Is a swim cap required at this pool?
items.passage: A sign at the pool says, "Everyone must wear a swim cap. No cap, no swimming."
items.hint: Can you swim there without a cap?
items.explanation: Yes. "Must wear" and "No cap, no swimming" mean a cap is necessary. When something is necessary, it is required.

items.prompt: Which line uses require correctly?

options.text: "This game requires batteries, so we don't need any."
"This game requires batteries, so let's buy some."
"I require a nap right now, but I'm not tired at all."

items.hint: If something is required, you need it.
items.explanation: If the game requires batteries, it needs them, so buying some makes sense. Saying you don't need something that is required contradicts the meaning.

wrong.a: Requires means needs, so "we don't need any" contradicts it.
wrong.c: If you are not tired, you do not really need a nap.

words.definition: an answer to a problem, or a way to fix it

hero.text: When the bridge washed out, Nova's solution was to fly the stranded students across one at a time.

words.everyday: Our class found a solution to the messy lunchroom: a cleanup chart with jobs that rotate each week.

contrast.nonExample: Every morning, Leo complains that the bus is too crowded, but he never suggests a fix.
contrast.explanation: Complaining only describes the problem. A solution is a way to fix it.

items.prompt: What does solution mean in this sentence?
items.passage: Putting a rubber doorstop under the door was a simple solution to the slamming noise.

options.text: a way to fix a problem

items.hint: The doorstop stopped the slamming. What did it do to the problem?
items.explanation: A solution is a way to fix a problem. The doorstop fixed the problem of the slamming door.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The math problem seemed impossible, but Jada kept working until she found the ___.
items.clue: math problem; kept working until
items.hint: What do you find at the end of solving a math problem?
items.explanation: Jada "kept working until" she reached the end of the "math problem." The answer to a problem is its solution. She already had the question.

items.prompt: Is the drip hose a solution?
items.passage: The garden kept drying out, so the family set up a drip hose that waters the plants every morning.
items.hint: Does the hose fix the problem of the dry garden?
items.explanation: Yes. The problem was a dry garden, and the hose fixes it by watering the plants. A way to fix a problem is a solution.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what solution means.

chunks.text: To stop the puppy from chewing shoes,
to give him his own chew toys.
to leave more shoes on the floor.

items.hint: A solution makes the problem go away.
